toolset: The .NET SDK host (dotnet msbuild). Counts depend on this: severity comes from MediaPortal\.editorconfig, but the inventory also depends on which target frameworks the host builds and analyses, so it is NOT comparable with a full Visual Studio MSBuild log (that host sees fewer target frameworks and applies its own rule sets). See README.md, "Which build host, and why it matters".
note: Per-code warning floors for the .NET SDK host (dotnet msbuild). Regenerate with: .\scripts\ci\warnings.ps1 -UpdateBaseline   # after build.ps1 -Solution Server -Ratchet. Floor is a ceiling: a code missing from this file has budget 0.

notes.CS0618: Obsolete-API usage: 4 -> 0. Removed with the code that used it: the two MediaPortal.Common.Utils\Wmi\*.cs files (System.Management) and Setup\TVEngine\Win32ExceptionExtension.cs. Re-introducing an obsolete API call is a build failure on purpose - obsolete means "will break when the platform shrinks", which is what this project is doing.
notes.MSB3270: ProcessorArchitecture mismatch: 2 -> 0. The two warnings came from MediaPortal.TvEngine.Interfaces/Runtime, whose referenced TV assemblies (TvBusinessLayer, TvControl, TVDatabase, TvLibrary.Interfaces, TvThumbnails) are compiled x86 - the only x86-compiled managed dependencies in the tree. The whole TV service layer (SlimTv.Service3/3.5, Interfaces, Runtime, DB\SQLServer, Resources, Client, TvMosaicClient, the TvEngine setup bits and MP2-TVServerClientSetup) was deleted on 2026-10-18, which removes both warnings, the x86 anchor, the Gentle provider (which pinned net48) and ~7200 lines. Re-enabling MSB3270 means someone re-added an x86 assembly. See "The TV service layer is gone" in scripts\ci\README.md.
notes.CA1416: PlatformGuard: member is platform-unsupported. 366 with or without the WmiWin32ProcessWrapper exclusion in PlatformExcludedAttributes.txt. The one code that is identical on every host and platform (Visual Studio 366, .NET SDK host 366, Linux container 366) - which is exactly why it is the port metric and the one rule pinned to "warning" in MediaPortal\.editorconfig for all hosts and configurations.
notes.CA1063: Old count 78, new floor 832. Raised 2026-10-18 when analyzer severity moved into MediaPortal\.editorconfig and the Visual-Studio-only rule set names ("AllRules.ruleset" / "MinimumRecommendedRules.ruleset") were cleared in Source\Directory.Build.targets. Those rules used to be configured only inside Visual Studio, so a rule now fires on every host and on every target framework leg instead of only on some. Measured on identical source with this baseline flow: Visual Studio MSBuild 17.14 gave 1776 warnings before the change and 2322 after it, the .NET SDK 10.0.402 host gives 2330, and the two hosts now differ on exactly two codes (CA2024 +4 and NETSDK1138 +4, both from the SDK having newer targets/analyzers). All compiler-emitted codes (CS*, SYSLIB*) are identical between hosts, and CA1416 is 366 everywhere: on Visual Studio, on the SDK host, and in the Linux container. Eight rules moved this way, with measured before -> after: CA1063 78 -> 832, CA1401 4 -> 228, CA1065 2 -> 200, CA2213 10 -> 180, CA1001 6 -> 176, CA2101 2 -> 88, CA1060 2 -> 72, CA2200 6 -> 12. None of these is new debt; they were always there and previously unreported outside Visual Studio. They are real code-quality findings, so each is now capped at its own floor instead of being silently off.

notes.CA2021: Newly reported (invalid cast of an IEnumerable element type): floor 8 is a starting backlog, not a licence. Each of these is a real bug class.
notes.CA2022: Newly reported (stream read whose byte count is discarded - a silent short read): floor 14, same intent as CA2021.
notes.CA2024: Newly reported (Stream.Length used in an async path, which blocks a thread): floor 4. Emitted only by the .NET SDK host (Visual Studio 17.14 reports 0 here), because the rule comes from the SDK analyzer set - the reason this baseline is generated with -BuildHost Dotnet.
notes.NETSDK1138: The toolchain saying out loud that net6.0 is out of support (EOL 2024-11-12). Floor 4, and it appears only on the .NET SDK host (Visual Studio 17.14 reports 0). This is the retarget todo (p1-2-retarget) made audible; it should reach zero when the tree moves to net10.0.
